studies.title: The Effect of Processing Parameters and Calcium-stearate on the Ejection Process of Injection Molded Poly(Lactic Acid) Products
studies.materialContext: Poly(lactic acid) injection-moulded tensile specimens; calcium-stearate evaluated as a demoulding agent.
studies.toolContext: Mould with low draft angle and varying cavity width along the flow path.
measuredSignals: ejector force over 30 continuous injection-moulding cycles
processing parameters including injection rate, holding pressure/time, mould temperature, melt temperature, back pressure, screw speed and pre-process drying
studies.supports: Processing conditions and interfacial/mould-release behaviour can materially alter ejection load and demoulding damage risk.
studies.limitation: PLA, the tested mould geometry and calcium-stearate result are application-specific; they do not define universal eject-force, additive, draft-angle or process limits.

studies.title: Self-Assembled Monolayers of Alkanethiols on Nickel Insert: Characterization of Friction and Analysis on Demolding Quality in Microinjection Molding
studies.materialContext: Polymer microinjection moulding against nickel inserts with different self-assembled-monolayer anti-adhesion treatments.
studies.toolContext: Nickel microstructured insert; surface chemistry modified to alter adhesion/friction and release quality.
physicalQualityOutcomes: microstructure replication quality after injection moulding
studies.supports: Interfacial surface state and friction/adhesion behaviour can alter demoulding quality and repeatability of replicated microstructures.
studies.limitation: Microstructured nickel inserts and the tested SAM coatings are specialist conditions; measured friction/replication response does not define universal surface-treatment or ejection settings.

supportingStudy.title: Adhesion-Induced Demolding Forces of Hard Coated Microstructures Measured with a Novel Injection Molding Tool
supportingStudy.use: Supporting force-measurement evidence; not required to reach the two-study minimum in this dossier.
supportingStudy.limitation: PET, coating, insert geometry and adhesion-force configuration are specific to the experiment.

promotionClaim: Promote the mechanism-level statement that demoulding/ejection response is governed by interacting thermal contraction, friction/adhesion, surface/tool state and process history, and should be diagnosed with measured release/ejection signals plus physical part-quality evidence. Do not promote any study-specific numerical setting or coating/additive recommendation as universal guidance.
